3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: We were here for a significant meeting about the L-1 project. Several construction companies sent their representatives to the city hall.

6.speaker: Gus Manger
6.text: “That is a given. But we'll also see improvements in everything from logistics to growth. You made the right choice for sure.”

7.speaker: Symon Holl
7.text: “I came by train yesterday and it was a little uncomfortable. Besides starting our economic recovery, this project will make the journey here much more pleasant, Mr. President.”

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: We arrived in Anrica by train. After being greeted by crowds of cheering citizens and the local government officials, we headed to the city hall.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Even though Lileas Graf couldn't make the meeting, I had Symon Holl and Gus Manger by my side.

11.speaker: Symon Holl
11.text: “I am glad to hear that. We should be able to slow down the recession if we finish this project successfully.”

12.speaker: Gus Manger
12.text: “This project will help along my rural development plans by attracting new businesses to the area. Thank you.”

13.speaker: Symon Holl
13.text: “I have the overview of the companies here.”

14.speaker: Gus Manger
14.text: “I reviewed the listed corporations. I also wrote down some notes and ideas.”

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Symon handed the files over to me.

32.speaker: Symon Holl
32.text: “The respected Sordish State Corporation, also known as the SSC, was founded in 1891.”

33.speaker: Symon Holl
33.text: “The real estate and construction giant was founded in 1925 and expanded during the economic boom of the '30s.”

34.speaker: Symon Holl
34.text: “Taurus Holding was founded in 1946 and is owned by the entrepreneur Geralt Fais.”

37.speaker: Symon Holl
37.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_InT_Listened_SordishStateCorp"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_InT_Listened_TaurusHolding"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_InT_Listened_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false

38.speaker: Gus Manger
38.text: “The SSC is the primary reason why our current infrastructure is outdated. We need more adaptive construction companies.”

39.speaker: Gus Manger
39.text: “I had the chance to work with Underhall Construction in Holsord. They took several contracts for the central station renovation and excelled at it.”

40.speaker: Gus Manger
40.text: “They are a very interesting corporation, especially because of their innovative construction methods. But I don't think they're suitable for large projects like these.”

41.speaker: Gus Manger
41.text: “I am sure we will. According to your document many citizens will be employed because of business expansions.”

42.speaker: Symon Holl
42.text: “According to my estimations, the new railway will give about 50.000 citizens from the Greater Holsord and Gelsland areas employment.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “What will it take to stop the recession?”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “What kind of end results do we expect?”

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “Failure during this project is not an option.”

47.speaker: Symon Holl
47.text: “This is just the beginning. We will need to follow this project up with several other economic investments.”

48.speaker: Symon Holl
48.text: “Not as of right now. However, things might come up if the project doesn't go according to plan.”

49.speaker: Gus Manger
49.text: “You are right. We need to work together and think things through.”

50.speaker: Symon Holl
50.text: “Short-term employment and long-term economic development in the Gelsland and Greater Holsord regions.”

51.speaker: Gus Manger
51.text: “Which is dependent on our government budget, right?”

52.speaker: Gus Manger
52.text: “There are so many forgotten people living in the less developed areas between Lachaven and Holsord. They will benefit.”

53.speaker: Symon Holl
53.text: “Our economic revitalization plan is set to be a success. Failure is indeed not an option.”

54.speaker: Gus Manger
54.text: “I agree with Symon. Additional financial or political support might be necessary if certain parties or issues block us.”

56.speaker: Symon Holl
56.text: “They have experience, knowledge and manpower for a project this size. I'm not so sure about their efficiency, though.”

57.speaker: Gus Manger
57.text: “The Sordish State Corporation lacks a modern way of thinking. They also under-perform with their slow construction methods.”

58.speaker: Gus Manger
58.text: “There is also the fact that construction times are long. Which is mostly due to their outdated methods.”

59.speaker: Symon Holl
59.text: “I have no great admiration for the SSC, but their track record clearly shows completed contracts with thousands of employees who have experience.”

63.speaker: Gus Manger
63.text: “The disadvantage would be going against your election promises of moving away from a state-dominant economy.”

64.speaker: Symon Holl
64.text: “However, this would fulfil your initial election promise of using a state-dominant planned economy to improve the bleak recession situation.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “I am on the fence about the SSC.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “I like the SSC, but want to hear about the others.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “I would like to hear your thoughts, Symon.”

69.speaker: Symon Holl
69.text: “I think that they have been doing relatively well in the private sector, where they are dominating the construction industry with successful projects.”

70.speaker: Symon Holl
70.text: “Nonetheless, they subjected their workers to conditions below our working standards during the Holsord Central Station contract. Which is troubling.”

71.speaker: Gus Manger
71.text: “Having worked on the renovation project, I can say that the conditions were not bad. Extra effort was needed to finish it on time, which they did. That is all.”

72.speaker: Gus Manger
72.text: “Out of all three, this is the company I can trust. They work hard, long and fast to accomplish their contracts. They will get this done if we give it to them.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “I have settled on the SSC. [-2 Government Budget]”

74.speaker: Symon Holl
74.text: “I am not so sure about trusting them with such a big contract. Especially after certain issues surrounding the treatment of their workers. But at least they have worked on several mega-projects and always delivered on time.”

75.speaker: Gus Manger
75.text: “They worked on two infrastructure projects in Gelsland and one in Greater Holsord that were worth two billion Ren in total.”

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “I am not sure about Underhall Construction.”

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “Underhall seems interesting, but let's see the others.”

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “I have settled on Underhall Construction. [-2 Government Budget]”

86.speaker: Gus Manger
86.text: “To be frank, what was the largest mega-project they worked on? I don't even remember.”

87.speaker: Symon Holl
87.text: “Taurus has completed fewer projects than the other companies. However, they are slightly faster and cheaper.”

88.speaker: Symon Holl
88.text: “It would fit our election promises of switching to a free-market economy. Awarding contracts to privately owned corporations would be a step in the right direction.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “I don't feel confident about Taurus Holding.”

94.speaker: Gus Manger
94.text: “Exactly. And why take such a risk now? We need to play it safer with companies like Underhall. They've always delivered for the government on time.”

95.speaker: Symon Holl
95.text: “If we are going to try a different company, this one is the most unique.”

99.speaker: Symon Holl
99.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group won't like this, but the contract will be awarded to the Sordish State Corporation.”

100.speaker: Symon Holl
100.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group will be pleased. The contract will be awarded to Underhall Construction.”

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: It was time to make a decision about which company to award the L-1 High-Speed Railway contract to.

102.speaker: Symon Holl
102.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to Taurus Holding.”

103.speaker: Gus Manger
103.text: “No hard feelings, Mr. President. At the end of the day, the success of the project is what matters.”

104.speaker: Gus Manger
104.text: “You made the right choice. I can tell from my experience that we will be very satisfied with this company.”

105.speaker: Gus Manger
105.text: “No hard feelings, Mr. President. At the end of the day the success of the project is what matters.”

106.speaker: Symon Holl
106.text: “The company will be notified today, and construction work will begin immediately after.”

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: The meeting ended and we spent the remainder of the day attending events in Anrica.

110.speaker: Player
110.text: “I think we are off to a good start.”

111.speaker: Gus Manger
111.text: “It will be a pleasure to celebrate together. For now, I'll return to my duties and visit some foreign partners in Rizia. See you soon, Mr. President.”

112.speaker: Symon Holl
112.text: “My expectations are that the grand opening ceremony will be late next year.”

115.speaker: Symon Holl
115.text: “It is the main state corporation tasked with running the day-to-day construction services of our country.”

116.speaker: Symon Holl
116.text: “The CEO of Underhall is Kris Schar, the mayor of Conriat. He sold half of his shares a few years ago but seemed very eager about the L-1 bid.”

117.speaker: Symon Holl
117.text: “It is a new holding company whose subsidiaries use cutting-edge technology from Arcasia to reduce construction costs and prices. They are known to provide for their workers, who are part of the Labour Union of Sordland.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “We need to be able to trust the corporation. This is a base requirement for the contract.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “Working conditions must be respected. This doesn't inspire confidence.”

120.speaker: Gus Manger
120.text: "Let me just point out that some of the workers were Agnolian and Wehzek. Technically, Sordish labor laws didn't apply to them.”

121.speaker: Gus Manger
121.text: “I think their capabilities are very suitable for the L-1 Railway project.”

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “The lack of a dynamic attitude is disappointing.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “The regional railway system has no relation to this.”

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “The experience they bring to the table is beneficial.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “They do have a wealth of knowledge in infrastructure.”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “The innovative aspect is refreshing. Especially if they can deliver.”

127.speaker: Player
127.text: “It seems like they lack the necessary experience.”

128.speaker: Player
128.text: “We shouldn't put our first project at risk. There is too much at stake here.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “Their capabilities matter more than the history they have. We need to make unbiased decisions.”

130.speaker: Symon Holl
130.text: “Picking this corporation would fit our market economy policy.”

131.speaker: Symon Holl
131.text: “Picking this corporation would go against our planned economy policy.”

135.speaker: Symon Holl
135.text: “Good that we are staying consistent to our economic strategy.”

140.speaker: Symon Holl
140.text: “Good that we are staying consistent to our economic strategy.”

145.speaker: Symon Holl
145.text: “Good that we are staying consistent to our economic strategy.”

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: It was very refreshing to attend cultural dance events and hear the traditional Sordish music of the region.

151.speaker: Gus Manger
151.text: “Choosing this corporation is too risky for a project like this. What if things were to go wrong?”

152.speaker: Gus Manger
152.text: “Look at the abysmal regional railway system!”

153.speaker: Symon Holl
153.text: “They took a joint contract in Arcasia for restructuring the highway intersection of one of the major cities. It went well, but it is their only large-scale success.”

165.speaker: Symon Holl
165.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to Underhall Construction.”

166.speaker: Symon Holl
166.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group won't like this, but the contract will be awarded to Taurus Holding.”

167.speaker: Symon Holl
167.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to the Sordish State Corporation.”

168.speaker: Narrator
168.text: Symon signed a certain section of the dossier and fixed his glasses.

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: Symon signed a certain section of the dossier and fixed his glasses.

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: Symon signed a certain section of the dossier and fixed his glasses.

174.speaker: Narrator
174.text: Symon searched through the documents he was holding and found the one he was looking for.

175.speaker: Symon Holl
175.text: “It won several awards internationally for being one of the fastest growing and advanced companies.”

193.speaker: Symon Holl
193.text: “According to the preliminary calculations of the SSC, they would need more resources to finish a project of this size.”

194.speaker: Symon Holl
194.text: “Underhall has specifically mentioned their solid track record and highlighted that they do anticipate to go over budget, but that they will finish on time.”

196.speaker: Symon Holl
196.text: “The project manager from Taurus Holding mentioned that they would be able to finish the project with the allocated funding. They are the only company who found the budget sufficient, making them a cheaper alternative.”

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “I have settled on the SSC. [-1 Government Budget]”

207.speaker: Narrator
207.text: Gus was first to arrive. He greeted me with a heartwarming smile.

208.speaker: Gus Manger
208.text: “Hello Mr President. Good to see you again.”

209.speaker: Gus Manger
209.text: “Appreciate you taking up my offer on the stock investment. Armadine is a very promising corporation, and if everything goes well you will make solid returns.”

211.speaker: Player
211.text: “Thanks for arranging the opportunity. I'll treat you to a 30-year-old Erlory Maroon if they make solid profits.”

212.speaker: Gus Manger
212.text: “My pleasure, Mr. President. I'm looking forward to that Erlory Maroon already.”

213.speaker: Gus Manger
213.text: “One has to play the game to be able to win.”

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: Symon Holl joined us. After settling down, we moved on to discuss the details of the L-1 Railway project.

215.speaker: Player
215.text: “*If* being the key word. I might lose all the money I put in.”

216.speaker: Gus Manger
216.text: “The least likely scenario. You can trust me on these subjects.”

220.speaker: Gus Manger
220.text: “That's a big 'if', Mr. President. We need to play it safer with companies like Underhall. They've always delivered for the government on time.”
